code: library(balancesample)  set.seed(2026) n <- 300 d <- data.frame(   age = rgamma(n, shape = 4, rate = 0.1),   income = rlnorm(n, meanlog = 10, sdlog = 0.6),   diagnosis = factor(sample(     c("none", "mild", "severe"),     n,     replace = TRUE,     prob = c(0.6, 0.3, 0.1)   )),   site = factor(sample(c("A", "B", "C"), n, replace = TRUE)) ) severe <- d$diagnosis == "severe" d$outcome <- 0.05 * d$age + 0.3 * log(d$income) + 1.5 * severe + rnorm(n)

A tibble: 9 × 5 #>   id    variable  level  statistic     value #>   <chr> <chr>     <chr>  <chr>         <dbl> #> 1 Split age       NA     smd       -0.000105 #> 2 Split income    NA     smd        0.00133  #> 3 Split diagnosis mild   smd       -0.0373   #> 4 Split diagnosis none   smd        0.0339   #> 5 Split diagnosis severe smd        0        #> 6 Split site      A      smd       -0.0174   #> 7 Split site      B      smd        0.0367   #> 8 Split site      C      smd       -0.0174   #> 9 Split NA        NA     energy     0.0286 folds <- balanced_vfold_cv(   train,   v = 5,   balance = c(age, income),   exact = c(diagnosis, site) ) library(ggplot2) autoplot(balance_check(folds)) library(balancesample) library(parsnip) library(tune) library(workflows)  wf <- workflow(   outcome ~ age + income + diagnosis + site,   decision_tree(     tree_depth = tune(),     min_n = tune(),     mode = "regression"   ) ) res <- tune_grid(wf, resamples = folds, grid = 6) show_best(res, metric = "rmse", n = 3) #> # title: Get started with balancesample
text: balancesample four methods. keep exact counts. differ make sets similar balance columns: "anticlust" (default) uses k-plus anticlustering anticlust package (Papenberg, 2024). starts random assignment swaps rows exact stratum sets swap improves one score similar means variances sets . default, considers every row stratum swap partner, run time grows quickly number rows. "twinning" uses data twinning twinning package (Vakayil Joseph, 2022). takes one set data time. takes row nearest unused neighbours small group keeps first row set. next group starts unused row closest last group’s farthest neighbour, set covers data way whole data . within exact stratum. folds, default strategy repeats rows left. one test 10 folds, took 0.2 seconds 1,000 10,000 rows (see README). needs twinning package, allows split proportions, splits small strata random (folds, strata fewer 2 * v rows). "rerandomize" uses rerandomization (Morgan Rubin, 2012). draws stratified random splits scores one Mahalanobis imbalance: distance means sets takes correlations columns account. folds, score largest imbalance fold rest. keeps first draw scores cutoff, set 100 pilot draws 10% draws pass. none 1,000 draws passes, uses best one, warning. balances means , needs extra package. "interaction" cuts numeric column four bins rank, crosses levels categorical columns, stratifies random result. Within exact stratum, cells fewer 10% rows pooled. Crossed cells get small fast: , age income quartiles 9 exact strata, largest cell 8 rows cutoff 30, every cell pooled folds random within exact strata. baseline shows crossed strata become sparse. compares four full data 10 folds: run, anticlust smallest max_abs_smd (0.134), twinning smallest mean_energy (0.039). come one run method one data set, don’t show method best general, small differences may noise. Start anticlust. large data, set options = list(k_neighbours = 20) try twinning, check balance . README lists run times . See ?balanced_vfold_cv options method.
code: methods <- c("anticlust", "twinning", "rerandomize", "interaction") by_method <- lapply(methods, function(m) {   f <- balanced_vfold_cv(     d,     v = 10,     balance = c(age, income),     exact = c(diagnosis, site),     method = m   )   s <- summary(balance_check(f))   data.frame(     method = m,     max_abs_smd = max(s$max_abs_smd),     mean_energy = mean(s$energy)   ) }) by_method <- do.call(rbind, by_method) shown <- by_method shown[-1] <- round(shown[-1], 3) shown #>        method max_abs_smd mean_energy #> 1   anticlust       0.134       0.054 #> 2    twinning       0.205       0.039 #> 3 rerandomize       0.370       0.065 #> 4 interaction       0.378       0.070
